newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty seen appreciating 4.3 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty seen appreciating 4.3 pct in 1997.

text.p: The Polish zloty is expected to appreciate 4.3 percent in real terms in 1997, according to Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko.

Kolodko said on Wednesday that next year's expected 13 percent rise in consumer prices is likely to be accompanied by a 8.7 percent depreciation of the zloty against a basket of currencies, resulting in the real term rise of the Polish unit.

"For the next year, I expect prices to rise by about 13 percent and the zloty to depreciate about 8.7 percent against the basket of currencies. Real appreciation of the zloty will take place in this space," Kolodko told foreign reporters.
He did not say if this would be achieved by cutting the zloty's crawling peg devaluation factor, now at one percent per month, or by appreciation within its 14 percent trading band.

The zloty floats within its daily band, which is set around a parity rate calculated daily by the central bank according to the value of a basket of five western currencies, and the devaluation factor.
He said real term appreciation of the zloty should continue until 2000, bringing the average monthly income in Poland to between $500 and $600 from about $360 now.
"According to our policy the scale of the devaluation should be slightly less than expected inflation, this is the margin for zloty appreciation," Kolodko said.
The zloty appreciated about 10 percent in real terms from mid-1995 to the middle of this year on the back of huge current account surpluses including large cross-border trade inflows.
